title: Expedited offboarding waives the notice timeline but never the notices themselves
content:
A.3.7.1.5.4.1 provides that when "a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol," expedited offboardings "override the timeline specified in A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters."

A.3.7.1.5.4.2 then draws the line precisely: "The public announcements defined in A.3.7.1.5.2 must still be carried out. However, the timing of these announcements no longer constrains the modification of parameters. These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons."

The distinction separates two things the ordinary process bundles together. The 14-day windows are a *forbearance* — a promise not to act before users have had time to react — and forbearance is what an emergency legitimately overrides. The announcements are a *disclosure*, and disclosure has no cost that an emergency could justify skipping; if anything an emergency raises its value.

Two procedural safeguards keep the exception from swallowing the rule. A.3.7.1.5.4.1 requires that the Offboarding Proposal state the emergency ground, referencing the Atlas's own definition of emergency situations, and that it "explicitly reference this Atlas document." Invoking the fast path therefore leaves a citable record naming the authority used, which makes after-the-fact review of whether the emergency was real straightforward.

The added duty to explain the acceleration is the same instinct: users who lose the notice period are at least owed the reason.
description: In a security or solvency emergency all parameters may change immediately, yet the same public announcements must still be made and must state that the process was accelerated and why.
